test_policy.notes: Test-optional since 1969; applicants choose whether SAT/ACT scores are reviewed and can suppress scores until the application deadline. Both SAT and ACT are superscored. Self-reported scores accepted; scores verified for enrolling students.

requirements.notes: $70 fee, automatically waived for aid applicants and first-generation students. Bowdoin Supplement has only two optional short essays. Three recommendations: counselor, one academic teacher, and one 'other' (second teacher or a coach/employer/community member). Optional video response and optional independent interviews (InitialView / Vericant). International applicants (not Canadians) submit CSS Profile only after admission.

deadlines.label: Early Decision 1
deadlines.notes: Decision mid-December (no exact date published). Aid application also due Nov 15 for domestic applicants.

deadlines.label: Early Decision 2
deadlines.notes: Decision early February (no exact date published).

deadlines.label: Regular Decision
deadlines.notes: Decision mid-March (no exact date published). Domestic aid application due Feb 1.

english_policy.waiver_notes: Submitting an English proficiency test is optional and there is no minimum score; scores cannot be deleted once submitted. Accepted: TOEFL, IELTS, Duolingo English Test, Cambridge English. Bowdoin offers no ESL courses, so students are expected to be highly proficient in English.

english.notes: Optional (Cambridge English Assessment); no minimum score.

aid.notes: Need-blind for international students and meets the full calculated need of every admitted student, with no loans in aid packages. Beginning with the Class of 2031, international applicants (excluding Canadians) submit aid materials (CSS Profile, code 3089) only after being admitted. International transfer students are not eligible for institutional aid.

toefl.note: Bowdoin's pages list SAT and ACT codes only; no TOEFL code found on the pages checked.
